content:
maria: heads-up — our repo scanner flagged a commit on feature/eyeful that contains a .env with AWS keys. commit 9c4f1b. snippet: `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA...\nAWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=abcd...`
kevin: yikes. which user/role is that key tied to? could be long-lived local creds.
alex: that was my local test key, i accidentally committed before squashing. i'm on it to rotate. sorry. :grimacing: 
maria: ok — containment checklist (do these in order):
  1) revoke the exposed key immediately
  2) rotate / create new short-lived creds or assume-role for devs
  3) check CloudTrail for any activity from that key since commit time
  4) search CI/build logs and artifacts for leakage or usage
  5) block merges and pause CI for that branch until cleared
  6) run repo-history scrub (BFG) if the secret reached a public mirror or external party
jamie: adding: add a KMS-backed secret in SSM/Secrets Manager for local dev workflows, and enforce via pre-commit hooks + branch protection. also update runbook for rotating dev keys.
sec-bot: Automated detection: secret_scan:v2 matched pattern AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in sources/services/renderer/.env at commit 9c4f1b. Created ticket SEC-342.
kevin: alex — confirm once you revoke and push proof (screenshot of rotation or IAM command output). we need the exact AccessKeyId to revoke.
alex: revoking now. running:
```
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE123 --status Inactive --user-name alex
aws iam delete-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE123 --user-name alex
```
(already rotated with a new short-lived federated token for local dev)
jamie: good. next: search repo history and CI cache for that key. example commands:
```
# find any reference in git history
git log --all -p --grep='AKIA' --pretty=oneline
# search build artifacts in GCS/CI cache
gsutil -m grep -R "AKIAEXAMPLE" gs://redwood-ci-artifacts/
```
maria: i'll run an account-wide CloudTrail query for that AccessKeyId and paste results here. also checking if our build runners cached env files.
kevin: also check if the key was uploaded to any third-party integrations (sentry, rollbar, etc.).
sec-bot: Note: per policy, developer long-lived access keys are disallowed for prod account. Flagging for RBAC review.
jamie: postmortem actions to assign: add exception policy for OSS contributors, tighten developer IAM so keys can't be created without approval, add enforcement in terraform CI to reject plain-text secrets on push, and increase audit log retention for 90 days for faster retrospectives.
alex: updated PR with history scrub instructions and proof of key deletion. also added a pre-commit hook sample to .githooks/pre-commit that checks for AWS keys.
maria: quick status: CloudTrail shows no usage after commit timestamp -> looks like no exfil. CI artifact search returned one cached tarball with the .env in runner cache — we'll purge that cache and rotate any tokens used by those runners.
kevin: great. jamie, can you add a ticket for RBAC changes? we should scope: 1) disable long-lived keys by default, 2) require STS/assume-role for local dev, 3) enforce KMS envelope encryption for any stored secrets.
jamie: will do. also increasing pre-commit coverage in repo templates and updating the onboarding doc.
sec-bot: SEC-342 updated: containment=done, rotation=done, CI-cache-purge=pending, repo-scrub=pending.
alex: sorry again everyone. will follow the new flow.
maria: thanks. final items: we need a short blameless postmortem entry, update the secrets runbook with the commands we ran, and schedule a 30min retro with eng + sec to review the new dev secrets workflow. :white_check_mark:
